strategy.summary: Reproduce numpy/numpy#28595 by building NumPy at the buggy commit 250285f3cefd, applying the PR's test diff, and running the two new pytest tests test_inf_zeroes_err and test_nan_err in numpy/lib/tests/test_function_base.py. On the buggy revision np.quantile with inverted_cdf and degenerate weights (all zero, inf, nan, or overflowing sums) returns a value with a RuntimeWarning instead of raising ValueError, so pytest.raises fails with 'DID NOT RAISE'. On the fixed revision the NaN/inf/zero check raises ValueError matching 'Weights included NaN, inf or were all zero', so both tests pass. The test assertion is an exception type and message match, not a numeric comparison.

system_packages: C compiler (gcc or clang) and C++ compiler
build_commands: git apply <PR 28595 test diff restricted to numpy/lib/tests/test_function_base.py>
python -m pip install pytest hypothesis meson-python meson ninja cython
pinned_because: Python 3.13 is only the version reported in the issue environment; the evidence does not require it, so it is a choice and any Python version NumPy at this commit builds on would do.
pytest and hypothesis are documented in README.md with no version constraint and no era ceiling, so the latest releases compatible with the chosen Python are used.
hypothesis is needed at import time because test_function_base.py imports it for TestLerp, so collection fails without it.

Build backend packages (meson-python, meson, ninja, cython) come from the repository build-system requirements, not from the evidence; use the versions that pyproject.toml pins at this commit if it pins them.

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest numpy/lib/tests/test_function_base.py -k "test_inf_zeroes_err or test_nan_err" -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/lib/tests/test_function_base.py::TestQuantile::test_inf_zeroes_err (parametrized over weights in [1,inf,1,1], [1,inf,1,inf], [0,0,0,0], [finfo(float64).max]*4 and dtype f8/O) and numpy/lib/tests/test_function_base.py::TestQuantile::test_nan_err (parametrized over weights containing np.nan and dtype f8/O). The class name TestQuantile is inferred from the hunk location after test_closest_observation, not shown in the diff.
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision 250285f3cefd with the test diff applied: every parametrized case of test_inf_zeroes_err and test_nan_err fails, because np.quantile returns a value (with RuntimeWarning for the zero-weight case) and pytest.raises reports that no exception was raised. Fixed revision (the commit after PR 28595 is merged): the same selected tests all pass, because the new check raises ValueError with the message 'Weights included NaN, inf or were all zero'.
strategy.numerical_probe: None needed. The transition is decided by whether ValueError is raised, not by any numeric value; do not compare outputs.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: array(1) with RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in divide
input_output_examples.expected_output: ValueError raised (message: 'Weights included NaN, inf or were all zero.')

risks: The given test_command (python -c "import numpy; numpy.test()") does not select the new tests and must not be used; numpy.test is not a reliable entry point, and running from the repository root can import the source tree instead of the built package. Use the pytest command above.
The build must succeed from source at 250285f3cefd; an editable build needs a working C/C++ toolchain and the build backend packages, and failure there gives no transition at all.

Object-dtype (dtype 'O') cases may fail on the buggy revision for a different reason (e.g. TypeError or a different warning) rather than the missing ValueError. They still fail, but the failure reason should be checked, and the test_nan_err O case accepts (RuntimeWarning, ValueError) so a warning alone is not enough to pass on the fixed revision.

If the project's pytest configuration turns RuntimeWarning into an error, the buggy revision may raise RuntimeWarning instead of returning a value; the tests still fail there because pytest.raises(ValueError) does not match it, so the transition holds but the failure message differs.
The overflow case [finfo(float64).max]*4 relies on IEEE overflow when summing weights; this is platform-independent for float64 and does not need a special architecture or sanitizer.
The evidence does not show a platform, sanitizer, BLAS backend or threading requirement; none is assumed. The defect is a plain Python-level check in quantile, so no specific architecture is needed.
The test diff adds a blank line before class TestLerp, which is cosmetic and does not affect the transition.
Versions of pytest and hypothesis are not constrained by the evidence; the latest compatible releases are chosen, and a future incompatibility with this older NumPy commit could affect collection.

oracle.reference_source: PR #28595 diff and the reproducing test diff
oracle.why: The assertion is an exception type (ValueError) and a regex match on the message; no numerical tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision np.quantile with method inverted_cdf and degenerate weights returns a value (and a RuntimeWarning at cdf /= cdf[-1, ...]) rather than raising, so pytest.raises(ValueError, match=...) reports 'DID NOT RAISE' and the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the added check raises ValueError('Weights included NaN, inf or were all zero.') for all selected parametrizations, so pytest.raises matches and both tests pass.
